SAF produced outside of New England is expected to be delivered pre-blended with Jet A due to existing production volumes, terminal space constraints, infrastructure availability, and limitations in the ability of some terminals to receive fuel by multiple modes. Deliveries of SAF/Jet A blends results in business as usual for New England, with the infrastructure investment to handle SAF occurring upstream of New England. It is expected that a pre-blended SAF/Jet A fuel would either be blended in New York Harbor or along the Gulf Coast and delivered to New York Harbor via the Colonial Pipeline. Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport (BTV) received their first shipment of SAF/Jet A blend in April 2025, and their fixed-base operator confirmed that the fuel was blended in Texas, delivered to a New York Harbor-area terminal, and delivered by truck to BTV (Business Air News 2025). SAF produced in New England requires more consideration. A SAF biorefinery is not expected along the coast due to the high value of land. Therefore, local SAF production is expected to be delivered to terminals by truck or barge. The Energy Transfer terminal in East Boston, which viii This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. supplies the highest volume of Jet A in the region, cannot receive fuel by truck, only by barge, and space for additional tanks and associated infrastructure is limited. Therefore, other terminals were evaluated for their potential to handle locally produced SAF. A preferred terminal for blending SAF produced in New England would have the following attributes to reduce costs: • Located near a SAF production facility. • Currently stores jet fuel due to existing dedicated infrastructure to reduce capital costs. • Existing infrastructure to receive fuel by truck. • Existing infrastructure to offload fuel by both truck and marine. While the potential location of a regional SAF facility is unknown, Sprague Energy’s South Portland, Maine, and Quincy, Massachusetts, terminals both meet the other criteria. With additional equipment to offload to marine, Sunoco in South Portland, Maine would also be a suitable location.
